I graded `submissions/s2.json` and wrote `grades/0001-s2.json`. I also added learning record `0003` and updated `NOTES.md`. Riley got 3 of 6 correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model only writes the tool request, and this is better than the first attempt. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | Riley chose "left to run longer, it will eventually fix the bug". A repeating failure needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. s1 had this right. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | The count of 4 is right, but the reasoning says the model runs the tools. The program runs them, and the model only requests them. |
| q5 | correct | Both parts are there: the result goes back as the next input, so the model can decide what to do next. |
| q6 | partial | Riley said the model picks "by the name". The model uses the whole tool description, not just the name. |

**Summary for Riley:** You have the loop down, but your reasoning in q4 still says the model runs the tools (M4). You also need a stopping condition, because more steps don't fix a repeating failure (M6).

**Next step:** Trace the laser-cutter request again and label each line "model writes" or "program runs". Then say what stops the loop if `check_calendar` keeps failing. Do this before the context and memory lesson.

`submissions/s1.json` is still ungraded, as nobody asked for it.
